text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers.

- The board of directors of the Basle-based Bank of International Settlements invited central banks of Slovenia, Bosnia, Croatia and Macedonia to become shareholders of the bank ahead of reaching an agreement with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia on how to divide assets of the former federation.
- Railway workers held a four-hour strike on Tuesday but the management refused to meet their demands for higher pay.
- Parliament is expected to decide on Wednesday whether to take a vote on ratification of the association agreement with the European Union this week.
- Ljubljana city council voted against the dismissal of the director of city management Janez Sodrznik, who was accused of misusing his authority by the mayor, Dimitrij Rupel.
- About 62.7 percent of Slovenians believe Slovenia should join the EU, down from 67.8 percent in May last year and 78.4 percent in June 1994, an opinion poll showed.
- The interior ministers of Slovenia, Italy and Hungary signed an agreement in Rome on tighter cooperation in dealing with crime.

- The parliamentary legislation board is expected to decide whether the initiative of a group of citizens who called for a referendum on whether an association agreement with the EU should be ratified, is in line with Slovenian legislation.
- A group of 115 intellectuals called for an immediate ratification of the EU association agreement.
- Telephone firm Digitel complained to the Constitutional Court over the monopoly of the state-owned mobile telephone operator Mobitel.

- Insurers said an increase of around 10 percent in car insurance premium prices introduced last week will not be sufficient to cover last year's loss of about six billion tolars ($38.7 million) by the end of 1997.
